claude.result:
I fixed it: `frai gate init --ci` now creates `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml`. I rebuilt with `pnpm --filter frai build` and ran it in an empty folder, and it created both `FRAI-SPEC.md` and the workflow file.

**Cause:** the top-level `frai` command has its own `--ci` option. By default the command-line library (Commander) lets top-level options appear anywhere on the line, even after a subcommand. So it took `--ci` for itself, and `gate` only passed `init` on to `frai-gate`. No error was shown because the flag counted as valid.

**Fix** (`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`, two lines):
- I added `.enablePositionalOptions()` to the top-level command, so its options only count when they come before a subcommand.
- I added `.passThroughOptions()` to the `gate` command, so every flag after `gate` goes to `frai-gate` unchanged.

`packages/frai-gate` is untouched. `frai --version` and `frai scan --ci --json` still work.

**Side effect:** a top-level-only option placed after a different subcommand, like `frai index --global`, used to be silently ignored. It will now probably fail as an unknown option. No subcommand ever used those misplaced options, so nothing that worked before should break.

**Cleanup needed:** I ran the test in `.tmp-ci-test/` at the repo root, and deleting it was blocked by permissions. Please delete that folder (`rm -rf .tmp-ci-test`). I also couldn't run `git status` to check the working tree, and I haven't committed anything.
